'''Leslie Gary Leal''' (born March 18, 1943) is the Warren & Katharine Schlinger Professor of Chemical Engineering at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]], United States.<ref>[http://www.chemengr.ucsb.edu/people/faculty_d.php?id=17 L. Gary Leal] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110511090051/http://www.chemengr.ucsb.edu/people/faculty_d.php?id=17 |date=May 11, 2011}} at [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]</ref> He is known for his research work in the dynamics of [[complex fluids]].

Leal was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1987 for fundamental contributions to the understanding of the fluid mechanics of particulate systems, polymer solutions, and suspensions.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nae.edu/27836/Dr-L-Gary-Leal |title=Dr. L. Gary Leal |publisher=[[National Academy of Engineering]] |access-date=2024-06-17}}</ref>

==Career==
Leal received his B.S. degree from the [[University of Washington]] in 1965, M.S. degree from the [[Stanford University]] in 1968, and Ph.D. degree from the [[Stanford University]] in 1969; all in chemical engineering.<ref name="aip_leal">{{cite web|url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?leall|title=Array of Contemporary American Physicists &#124; L. Gary Leal|publisher=[[American Institute of Physics]]|accessdate=11 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121004213018/http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?leall|archive-date=4 October 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> His Ph.D. thesis advisor was [[Andreas Acrivos]]. He then spent two years at  the University of Cambridge, studying with [[George Batchelor|Professor G. K. Batchelor]].

Leal started his academic career in 1970 as an assistant professor in chemical engineering at [[California Institute of Technology]]. He became a full professor in 1978. During 1986–1989, he was Chevron Distinguished Professor of Chemical Engineering. In 1989, Leal joined University of California, Santa Barbara as professor and chair in the department of chemical engineering. He is currently the Warren and Katharine Schlinger Professor of Chemical Engineering Emeritus at [[University of California, Santa Barbara|UCSB]].<ref name="aip_leal" />

==Research==
Leal's research covers a wide range of topics in fluid dynamics, including the dynamics of complex fluids, such as polymeric liquids, emulsions, polymer blends, and liquid crystalline polymers. He also works on large-scale computer simulation of complex fluid flows. Leal and his coworkers made pioneering contributions to the study of drop deformation under different flow conditions. They have developed a scheme based on a [[finite difference method|finite difference approximation]] of the equations of motion, applied on a boundary-fitted orthogonal curvilinear coordinate system, inside and outside the drop.<ref name="Ryskin">{{cite journal|last=Ryskin|first=G.|author2=L. G. Leal |year=1984|title=Numerical Solution of Free-Boundary Problems in Fluid Mechanics. Part 1. The Finite-Difference Technique|journal=J. Fluid Mech.|volume=148|pages=1–17|doi=10.1017/S0022112084002214|bibcode = 1984JFM...148....1R |s2cid=340747 |url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/10116/1/RYSjfm84a.pdf}}</ref><ref name="Kang">{{cite journal|last=Kang|first=I. S.|author2=L. G. Leal |year=1987|title=Numerical Solution of Axisymmetric Unsteady Free-Boundary Problems at Finite Reynolds Number. I. Finite difference Scheme and its Application to the Deformation of a Bubble in a Uniaxial Straining Flow|journal=Phys. Fluids|volume=30|pages=1929–1940|doi=10.1063/1.866207|bibcode = 1987PhFl...30.1929K|issue=7 }}</ref> Leal has published more than 250 papers on [[fluid dynamics]]. He has directed 55 Ph.D. thesis in various topics in fluid dynamics. Several of his students have gone on to become professors at prestigious universities including [[Howard A. Stone|Howard Stone]] who is currently at Princeton and [[Gerald Fuller]] at Stanford. Leal comes from a long line of researchers that can be traced back from mentor to mentor all the way to Sir Isaac Newton.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://neurotree.org/neurotree/distance.php?username=guest&sessionid=&refresh=1&search1=L.+Gary++Leal&pid1=59075&search2=Isaac++Newton&pid2=24747&includepd=1&backonly=1&Update=Find+Connection | access-date= 6 March 2020 | title = Neurotree -- Connection from L. Gary Leal to Isaac Newton }}</ref>

==Editorships==
From 1998–2015 he served as co-[[editor-in-chief]] of ''[[Physics of Fluids]]'' with [[John Kim (professor)|John Kim]].<ref>{{citation |first1=John |last1=Kim |first2=L. Gary |last2=Leal |title=Editorial: Fifty years of ''Physics of Fluids'' |journal=Physics of Fluids |volume=20 |issue=1 |pages=010401–010401–5 |year=2008 |doi=10.1063/1.2832366|bibcode=2008PhFl...20a0401K |s2cid=122376358 }}</ref>
